content.rendered:
If anyone is in Christ, the new creation has come. The old has gone. The new is here. Not a refurbished version of the old self. A new creation entirely. This is who you are.

The Gospel For Today | Monday, June 29, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, the new creation has come: The old has gone, the new is here!”
2 Corinthians 5:17 (NIV)

Today’s Message

Paul writes 2 Corinthians 5 to a church in a culture obsessed with self-improvement. The Greco-Roman world of the first century was filled with philosophies promising to make people better versions of themselves through discipline, education and moral effort. Into that environment, Paul drops a sentence that overturns the entire framework. The believer in Christ is not an improved version of the old self. The believer in Christ is a new creation.

The Greek phrase Paul uses is kainē ktisis. Kainē means new in kind, not just new in time. A new winter coat is new in time. The same kind of coat, just freshly bought. A new species of bird, however, is new in kind. Something that did not exist before. Paul says the believer is kainē. New in kind. A category of being that did not exist before the moment they were placed in Christ.

This is the foundation of the entire Christian life. Every command in the New Testament, every promise, every instruction, every comfort, assumes this new creation reality first. The believer is not being asked to become someone new. The believer is being invited to walk in who they already are. The old has gone. The new is here. Past tense. Completed action. Settled reality.

Practically, this changes everything. When you fail today, the response is not “I have to start over.” The response is “I am a new creation and that has not changed.” When you doubt your standing with God, the response is not “I need to earn my way back.” The response is “I am in Christ and the old me is gone.” When the enemy whispers that you are still the person you used to be, the response is not negotiation. The response is the Word. The old has gone. The new is here. That is who I am.

This is the first truth of the next fourteen days. Welcome to a new series of “The Gospel For Today” focused on identity in Christ. Over the next two weeks, we will be walking through the “I am” statements of the New Testament that describe who the believer already is by virtue of being in Christ. Today we begin where Paul began. You are a new creation. The old has gone. The new is here. Walk in it today.

Prayer

Father, I acknowledge that I am a new creation in Christ. The old has gone. The new is here. I am not an improved version of who I used to be. I am a new kind of being entirely, created in Christ Jesus. This is who I am today. The old life, with all its labels, failures and patterns, has been crucified with Christ. The new life I now live is by faith in the Son of God. I walk in this reality today, settled, free and at home in who You have made me to be. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

I am a new creation in Christ. The old has gone. The new is here. I am not who I used to be. I am who Christ has made me. I walk in newness of life today.
